signals.title: Lenny's Podcast: The rise of Cursor, with Michael Truell (co-founder and CEO)
signals.summary: The CEO discussed Cursor reaching $300M ARR and explained why it builds its own custom models (e.g. for autocomplete) alongside foundation models.

signals.title: Cursor 1.0: Bugbot, Background Agent access to everyone, and one-click MCP install
signals.summary: Cursor 1.0 launched Bugbot (automatic PR review on GitHub), opened the remote Background Agent to all users, and added a beta Memories feature that stores per-project facts from conversations.

signals.title: Series C and Scale: $900M at $9.9B valuation
signals.summary: Cursor raised $900M at a $9.9B valuation from Thrive, Accel, Andreessen Horowitz and DST, citing ARR above $500M and use by more than half of the Fortune 500.

signals.title: Clarifying our pricing
signals.summary: Cursor apologized for poorly communicated changes that moved Pro from 500 requests/month to token-based usage ($20 of frontier-model usage at API rates plus unlimited Auto), and offered refunds for unexpected charges from June 16 to July 4.

signals.title: Introducing Cursor 2.0 and Composer
signals.summary: Cursor shipped Composer, its first in-house coding model, plus a redesigned agent-centric interface that runs multiple agents in parallel via git worktrees or remote machines.

signals.title: Past, Present, and Future: $2.3B Series D at $29.3B post-money
signals.summary: Cursor raised $2.3B at a $29.3B post-money valuation with Coatue, NVIDIA and Google as new investors, reporting over $1B annualized revenue and 300+ employees; funds go to research.

signals.title: Graphite is joining Cursor
signals.summary: Cursor reached a binding agreement to acquire code review platform Graphite, framing review and merging as the new bottleneck; Graphite continues operating independently with planned product integration.

signals.title: Brian McCarthy joins Cursor as President of Global Revenue and Field Operations
signals.summary: Cursor announced Brian McCarthy, previously President and CRO at Rubrik, as President of Global Revenue and Field Operations leading its global go-to-market organization; the announcement cited use by more than 50,000 engineering teams and nearly 70% of the Fortune 1000 as customers.

signals.title: The third era of AI software development
signals.summary: CEO post arguing development is moving from Tab and synchronous agents to autonomous cloud agents; states 35% of internally merged PRs come from agents in cloud VMs and agent users now outnumber Tab users about 2:1.

signals.title: Introducing Composer 2
signals.summary: Composer 2, built with Cursor's first continued-pretraining run plus long-horizon RL, scored 61.3 on CursorBench (vs 44.2 for Composer 1.5) and is priced at $0.50/$2.50 per million input/output tokens; a technical report was released.

signals.title: Meet the new Cursor (Cursor 3)
signals.summary: Cursor 3 introduced an agent-first workspace showing local and cloud agents (started from desktop, web, mobile, Slack, GitHub, Linear) in one sidebar, with local/cloud handoff and a plugin marketplace.

signals.title: Cursor partners with SpaceX on model training
signals.summary: Cursor said it was compute-constrained and would use SpaceXAI's Colossus infrastructure to scale training of its Composer models; no financial terms were given in the post.

signals.title: Simon Green named Cursor President for Asia Pacific and Japan
signals.summary: Former Palo Alto Networks executive Simon Green was named APJ President to run go-to-market and set up a Singapore regional headquarters, targeting Japan, Australia and New Zealand, South Korea, India, Indonesia and Singapore.

signals.title: Bugbot is over 3x faster, 22% cheaper, and finds 10% more bugs
signals.summary: Bugbot, now powered by Composer 2.5, averages about 90 seconds per review (down from about 5 minutes) and adds a /review command to run Bugbot and Security Review locally before pushing.

signals.title: Cursor chooses London as EMEA headquarters, targets about 200 regional staff by end of 2026
signals.summary: Pulse 2.0 reported Cursor will open a London headquarters this summer and grow to about 200 EMEA employees by end of 2026, hiring across engineering, go-to-market, customer success and operations; SVP of EMEA Ismail Elmas is quoted.

signals.title: Cursor Mobile App for iOS
signals.summary: Public beta on paid plans for launching, monitoring and steering cloud agents from a phone, with push notifications, review of diffs and demos, and merging PRs.

signals.title: Cursor Router: Auto mode now routes each request to a suited model
signals.summary: Auto mode is powered by Cursor Router with Intelligence, Balance and Cost modes; admins can enable it per team, restrict modes and allow or block underlying models, and it is on by default for Teams plans.

signals.title: Cursor Start: INR 649/month plan for developers in India
signals.summary: Cursor launched an India-specific monthly plan at Rs 649 (tax inclusive) with UPI payment, including Grok and Composer models, always-on cloud agents and Cursor for iOS with remote control.

signals.title: Mixture-of-Kittens: open-source MoE training megakernel (Apache-2.0)
signals.summary: Cursor open-sourced a fused MoE communication-and-compute kernel for NVL72 racks that it says powers Composer training; it reports up to 2.37x kernel speedup and 1.41x end-to-end tokens/sec/GPU on 512 GPUs, with an arXiv paper (2609.36070).

signals.title: How Cursor Router chooses the right model for the task
signals.summary: Cursor described its router, which uses a complexity predictor and a task taxonomy built from live traffic; it states Auto Balance beats Opus 4.8 at 41% lower cost and that a frontier model is eligible for a task type only if it clears a one-sided 75% uplift threshold.

signals.title: Introducing Grok 4.6
signals.summary: Cursor and SpaceXAI released Grok 4.6, focused on long-running agents, available in Cursor, Grok Build and the SpaceXAI API at $2/$6 per million input/output tokens.

signals.title: Cursor reportedly to open first India office by end of 2026 and is hiring in Bengaluru region
signals.summary: Inc42, citing Moneycontrol, reported APJ head Simon Green saying Cursor will be in physical locations in India before year end; hiring has started for AI deployment, partnership management and field engineering roles, many on-site in Greater Bengaluru.

signals.title: Firetiger joins Cursor
signals.summary: The team of Firetiger, which builds agents that monitor rollouts, catch regressions and investigate incidents in production, joined Cursor as part of an investment in long-running autonomous agents.

signals.title: Cursor earns AIUC-1 certification for agent security and reliability
signals.summary: Cursor said it passed AIUC-1 after an independent audit by Schellman and adversarial testing of the IDE and cloud agents; it must be tested at least quarterly with a full annual audit.

signals.title: Cursor is now a part of SpaceX
signals.summary: Cursor announced it has been acquired by SpaceX, completing a process that began with the April model-training partnership; the post cites access to a very large GPU fleet and does not state deal terms.

signals.title: Origin Code Hosting enters early beta on paid plans
signals.summary: Cursor began rolling out Origin, its own code hosting with repos, pull requests, code browsing and two-way GitHub sync, with Vercel, Depot and Buildkite integrations.

signals.title: Git at any scale (Cursor Origin / Continuity)
signals.summary: Cursor described Origin, its Git hosting platform, built on a new storage system (Continuity) that logs pushes to S3-compatible object storage; it serves Git protocol, web UI, REST API and agent interactions.

signals.title: IMDEX uses Cursor to build integrated subsurface data and analytics platform
signals.summary: Cursor's case study says Australian mining-technology firm IMDEX built its data platform in 8 months and completed an Angular-to-React migration in 6 months, versus multi-year estimates without Cursor.

signals.title: Run cloud agents on machines you manage (Self-Hosted Machines)
signals.summary: Cloud agents can now execute tools on customer-managed machines or autoscaling worker pools while inference stays in Cursor's cloud; Cursor says cloud agents now create over 60% of its internally merged PRs.

signals.title: Nokia analyzes 50M+ lines of code in two weeks with Cursor
signals.summary: Cursor's case study says two Nokia engineers analyzed over 50 million lines of code in two weeks, a task expected to take a dozen-plus experts several months; Nokia is also using Cursor across early SDLC work.

signals.title: How Basis builds long-horizon accounting agents with Cursor
signals.summary: Basis, which builds agents for accountants and is trusted by 40% of the top 25 accounting firms per the post, says its agents complete partnership tax returns up to 6x faster.

signals.title: Introducing Projects
signals.summary: Projects (beta) are long-running cloud workspaces where a coordinator agent delegates to parallel subagents, keeps shared context files that persist across agents, and can subscribe to Slack, schedules or PRs.

signals.title: How Grab put Cursor in the hands of Design, Ops, and Engineering
signals.summary: Cursor's case study reports about 98% of Grab's tech organization uses Cursor monthly and over a third of merge requests incorporate it; figures are the vendor's account.

signals.title: Bots for the last mile: Rollouts, Security Review
signals.summary: Rollouts monitors changes from PR to production against telemetry (Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb) and can pause rollouts or open revert PRs; Security Reviewer flags vulnerabilities on every PR. Available on Teams and Enterprise.

signals.title: Improved token efficiency for longer agent runs
signals.summary: Agent harness changes (system prompt trimmed about 66%, built-in tools moved to dynamic context, cache breakpoints) cut user token costs 7% with no loss in agent quality, per Cursor.

signals.title: Remote control for local agents
signals.summary: Users can view and reply to local agents running on their computer from the Cursor iOS app; enabled by default except for Enterprise organizations, where admins can turn it on.

signals.title: Careers page: model training and agent infrastructure roles
signals.summary: As observed on 2026-10-12, the 34 open engineering roles include Pretraining, RL Data, RL Environments, Synthetic Data, ML Research/Platform/Infrastructure, Model Routing & Inference, Agent Harness, Evals, Bugbot and Grok Connectors.

signals.title: Careers page: enterprise go-to-market build-out
signals.summary: As observed on 2026-10-12, 134 roles are open, of which 40 are Sales (including federal, healthcare, life sciences and APJ enterprise) and 25 are Solutions (forward-deployed and field engineers), compared with 34 in Engineering.

timeMachine.announcement: Introducing Projects: coordinator agent delegating to parallel subagents with persistent shared context
timeMachine.why: Per-project Memories (June 2025), parallel agents in 2.0 (Oct 2025), the CEO's 'third era' post on autonomous cloud agents (Feb 2026, which the Projects post itself cites), and Cursor 3's unified local/cloud agent workspace (Apr 2026) each laid groundwork for long-running, multi-agent, memory-backed Projects.

timeMachine.announcement: Bots for the last mile: Rollouts and Security Review
timeMachine.why: Bugbot (June 2025) and the Graphite acquisition (Dec 2025) showed a push past code writing into review; the Firetiger acqui-hire (Aug 2026), a team building production-monitoring agents, preceded the Rollouts launch by about six weeks, and the launch post was written by Firetiger's co-founder.
